overview: Two major gene-silencing/editing tools with very different mechanisms — one permanently edits DNA, the other transiently reduces gene expression.
genZNote: CRISPR rewrites the book. RNAi just tears out pages temporarily.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A programmable gene-editing system using a guide RNA and the Cas9 nuclease to make precise, permanent cuts in DNA.
aspects.valueB: A post-transcriptional gene-silencing mechanism using small RNAs (siRNA/shRNA) to degrade or block specific mRNA transcripts.

aspects.label: Level of Action
aspects.valueA: Acts at the DNA level, permanently altering the genome.
aspects.valueB: Acts at the mRNA level, transiently reducing protein expression without altering the genome.

aspects.label: Permanence of Effect
aspects.valueA: Permanent and heritable — the edited DNA sequence is passed to daughter cells.
aspects.valueB: Transient and reversible — effects fade as the silencing RNA is degraded or diluted.

aspects.label: Mechanism
aspects.valueA: A guide RNA directs Cas9 to a complementary DNA sequence, where it introduces a double-strand break, repaired by NHEJ or HDR.
aspects.valueB: Double-stranded RNA is processed by Dicer into siRNA, loaded into the RISC complex, which degrades complementary mRNA.

aspects.label: Applications
aspects.valueA: Gene knockout/knock-in, correcting disease-causing mutations, generating model organisms.
aspects.valueB: Functional gene knockdown studies, and as a therapeutic strategy (e.g. siRNA drugs like patisiran).

aspects.label: Off-Target Considerations
aspects.valueA: Off-target genomic cutting is possible and a major safety/design concern.
aspects.valueB: Off-target silencing of similar mRNA sequences can occur, though effects are reversible.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Permanently edits the DNA sequence itself.
aspects.valueB: Temporarily silences gene expression at the RNA level.
